title: Tidy PostSchema
bug: Posts longer than 140 characters (allowed: 280) are rejected.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description only mentions reordering fields and tidying validators, but the diff changes the max text length from 280 to 140, which alters validation behavior for clients.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR silently reduces the maximum post text length from 280 to 140 characters without announcing this behavior change.

personas.goal: Send bad input to test validation

personas.goal: Probe s3: run flask fake posts and observe validation failures

personas.name: round2 probe-s1-create-long-post
personas.goal: Test that creating a post with text longer than 140 characters returns a 400 validation error.

personas.name: round2 probe-s2-update-long-post
personas.goal: Test that updating a post with text longer than 140 characters returns a 400 validation error.

personas.name: round2 probe-s3-fake-posts-cli
personas.goal: Test that the fake posts CLI command generates posts with text up to 280 characters which may now fail validation.

suspicions.evidence: Probe 'round2 probe-s2-update-long-post' created a post then sent PUT /api/posts/151 with 150-character text; both base and head returned 200 with the updated post, showing the update was accepted rather than rejected with a 400 validation error.

suspicions.claim: The fake posts CLI command still generates post texts up to 280 characters, which will now fail validation when the app runs with the new schema.
suspicions.trigger: Run `flask fake posts 10` in the app context. Observe that the command may raise validation errors or fail to commit posts because generated text exceeds the new 140-character limit.
suspicions.evidence: No probe executed the CLI command `flask fake posts`; all probes only used HTTP endpoints, so there is no evidence about whether the CLI command generates over-long texts.
